analysis.title: Shell Plc (SHEL.AS): Strong Q3 OCF and buyback, while upgrading portfolio and extending reserve life; Buy
key_insights: Shell 3Q26 post-tax operating profit was US$11,534 mn, 4% above company-compiled consensus of US$11,068 mn. Adjusted CCS earnings were US$10,814 mn, 5% above consensus of US$10,329 mn.

Cash flow from operations before working capital changes was US$21.7 bn, 19% above consensus of US$18.2 bn, driven by adjusted EBITDA and US$3.4 bn of net cash inflows from derivatives. Capex of US$7.9 bn left US$13.8 bn of FCF (pre-OWC).

Shell announced a US$5.0 bn buyback after completing the US$4.2 bn program announced at 2Q26. The new program is up from US$3.0 bn previously expected. Management called the extra US$2 bn a 'top-up' to keep pace with its 40-50% through-cycle CFFO distribution framework.
Net debt fell to US$39.7 bn at end 3Q26 from US$41.7 bn at 2Q26. Gearing (net debt/equity) fell to 20% from 23%, against GS estimate of 21%.

GS describes Shell's balance sheet as among the strongest in its Big Oils coverage, with no hybrids and almost no off-balance sheet project financing. 2026E net debt/capital employed is 10% vs a 14% European Oils average.

GS models a 4.6% buyback yield and a 2.8% dividend yield for 2026, a total shareholder yield of 7.5% vs the EU Oils average of 7.4%. 2026E breakevens are $4/bbl for the dividend and $35/bbl for dividend plus buyback, among the lowest in the sector.

Tanker freight rates are up 10-50x across all tanker classes since the start of the year, reaching up to c.$40/bbl on the longest hauls. Shell's leased tanker fleet and trading capability give it vessel access and the ability to redirect cargoes, which GS sees as an advantage into 4Q, especially in LNG.

Freight cost exposure is high for Shell in GS's screen: shipping cost of $15.8/bbl now vs $1.2/bbl a year ago, an increase of $14.6/bbl, ranked 13th of 15 producers. North Sea and US-weighted producers are less affected.
Shell closed the ARC Resources acquisition in 3Q26, adding ~370 kboe/d of production in Montney gas and liquids near LNG Canada. Production CAGR guidance rose to ~4% to 2030 vs 2025.

LNG Canada Phase 2 reached FID in 3Q26 and is expected online in 2030. GS says this implies a 90% organic reserve replacement ratio YTD, closing the gap with peers. Bonga Southwest in Nigeria could reach FID next year if conditions align.
GS's Top Projects database shows >500 kboed of new production through 2028 and c.$6 bn of cash flow potential from new projects over 2025-28.

FY2026 cash capex guidance was cut to US$23-25 bn (incl. c.$4 bn for ARC) from US$24-26 bn. Ex-ARC it is US$19-21 bn. Cumulative structural cost reductions reached US$5.8 bn after 1H26 against a US$5-7 bn target by end-2028.
Valuation: Shell trades at 4.6x 2026E EV/DACF, c.29% below its 20-year average, with a 2026E FCF yield of 16.2% vs EU Big Oils at 15.5%. 2026E P/E is 8.2x vs 12.3x 20-year average.

Q4 guidance: Integrated Gas production 1,080-1,180 kboe/d, LNG liquefaction 7.3-7.9 mt, upstream production 1,700-1,900 kboe/d, refinery utilisation 92-100%, and corporate adjusted earnings a net expense of $600-800 mn.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised from $123 to $129 after 3Q26 results, based on 6.0x EV/DACF on 2027E cash flow. Implied upside is 19.8% from $107.67.

sector_views.rationale: Shell is Buy rated on strong cash generation, balance sheet strength, low breakevens and project-driven production growth.

earnings_insights: Shell 3Q26 reported 10/29: post-tax operating profit US$11,534 mn vs company-compiled consensus US$11,068 mn (+4%). Adjusted CCS earnings US$10,814 mn vs consensus US$10,329 mn (+5%). GS's own estimate for post-tax operating profit was US$11,900 mn.

3Q26 segment results vs company-compiled consensus (all reported): Upstream US$3,189 mn vs US$3,094 mn consensus (+3%), Integrated Gas US$3,037 mn vs US$2,934 mn (+4%), Marketing US$1,164 mn vs US$1,149 mn (+1%), Chemicals and Products US$3,855 mn vs US$3,743 mn (+3%), Renewables and Energy Solutions US$289 mn vs US$148 mn.
3Q26 CFO ex-working capital was US$21,682 mn reported vs company-compiled consensus US$18,178 mn (+19%) and GS estimate of US$17,000 mn. Capex was US$7,922 mn vs GS estimate US$5,800 mn.

3Q26 results reflected high refining margins, high realised LNG prices and higher Integrated Gas volumes, partly offset by lower crude and oil products trading and optimisation, higher well write-offs and lower realised liquids prices.
Total oil and gas production in 3Q26 was 3,117 kboed, +27% qoq from 2,455 kboed, mostly from the ARC acquisition and lower maintenance. LNG liquefaction was 8.36 mt, +8% qoq.

GS EPS estimates (basic, pre-exceptionals, GS forecast): 2026E $6.72, 2027E $6.21, 2028E $5.15. Quarterly GS EPS forecasts are $1.73 (6/26), $1.93 (9/26) and $1.88 (12/26E). Reported 2025 EPS was $3.11.
3Q26 DPS was held flat qoq at US$0.3906 (+5% yoy). GS models a US$14.5 bn buyback in 2026 and 9% DPS growth, returning c.33% of CFO to shareholders.

trade_ideas.description: Buy Shell (SHEL.AS / SHEL) with 12-month price targets of €55.00 and $129.00
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong cash generation, balance sheet strength, shareholder distributions, integrated trading advantage and extended reserve life.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower oil and gas price realizations, especially European gas. Weaker recovery rates in mature offshore fields. Higher costs or capex. Materially lower cash returns to shareholders.

risk_factors: Lower oil and gas price realizations than expected, especially the European gas price, reducing earnings and cash flow.
Lower-than-expected recovery rates in mature offshore oil and gas fields, causing higher decline rates and lower production growth.
Higher-than-expected costs or capex in future developments.
Materially lower cash returns to shareholders, from a lower dividend or changed buyback guidance, after a commodity price downturn.
Higher freight costs are pressuring Shell's downstream margins.

Exhibit 20 shows Shell's 2026E P/E at 8.2x vs a 20-year average of 12.3x and EU Big Oils at 7.4x. Its 2026E EV/DACF is 4.6x vs 6.5x for the 20-year average and 4.5x for EU Big Oils.

theme_stances.key_argument: Shell can sustain both dividends and buybacks through a low oil price environment given its balance sheet and low breakevens.
theme_stances.evidence: one of the few companies that can maintain both buybacks and dividends

theme_stances.key_argument: Shell's leased tanker fleet and trading capabilities help it capture value from freight dislocations, even as higher freight costs weigh on downstream margins.
theme_stances.evidence: large managed tanker fleet provides security of vessel access
